name: colorcombinations
description: The Dictionary of Color Combinations — historically-grounded color palettes inspired by Sanzo Wada's 1933 Japanese color dictionary.

scripts.build: astro check && astro build && node scripts/make-worker.mjs
scripts._deploy_note: DEPLOY VIA CI, NOT FROM A LAPTOP (corrected 2026-09-03). Push to main and let .gitlab-ci.yml deploy; it runs `npx astro build` + `wrangler pages deploy` on GitLab runners and asserts the deployment reached production. MEASURED 2026-09-03: CI overwrote three local chunked deploys within ~3 minutes of each push (CF deployments c2da7fa0 commit 70cfb7a9 15:33 -> a4f5d839 DIRECT-UPLOAD 15:40 -> 56304e44 commit 3b8d6e4e 15:43, which is what went live), so a local chunked deploy is redundant work that is then discarded. NOTE the two paths are different BUILDS, not two ways to ship one: CI runs `npx astro build` and therefore never runs make-worker.mjs and never creates _worker.js, so wrangler compiles functions/ natively; `npm run build` DOES run make-worker.mjs and produces the advanced-mode _worker.js the chunked path needs. `npm run deploy` (the chunked path) remains correct ONLY as a fallback when CI is unavailable — it exists because dist is ~174MB across ~3,960 files and CF Pages closes the upload socket at a hard ~56MB PER CONNECTION, which kills raw `wrangler pages deploy` from a home uplink. Advanced mode did NOT break _redirects here: measured on the direct-upload deployment that actually carried _worker.js, /sitemap.xml and all 8 color-of-the-year rules still returned 301. Do not use /_worker.js to tell the two modes apart — it 404s in BOTH; the valid instrument is the CF deployments API trigger metadata (commit_hash present = wrangler/CI, absent = DIRECT-UPLOAD).
